summary: Kalamata Airport (KLX) is a regional airport serving the southern Peloponnese in Greece, acting as the main gateway to the Messenia region. It is situated about 8 km northwest of Kalamata city and handles both domestic flights and seasonal international charter services from European destinations. The airport supports tourism to popular nearby areas including the Mani Peninsula, Pylos, and the archaeological site of Ancient Messene.
faqs:
Q: How far is Kalamata Airport from the city center?
A: The airport is located approximately 8 km northwest of downtown Kalamata, with a typical drive time of around 15-20 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Are there international flights at Kalamata Airport?
A: The airport primarily handles seasonal international charter flights from various European cities during the summer tourist season, along with regular domestic flights to Athens.

Q: Does the airport operate year-round?
A: Yes, Kalamata Airport operates throughout the year, though international flight frequencies increase significantly between May and October.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The terminal offers standard amenities including a café, car rental desks, taxi services, and a small selection of duty-free and souvenir shops.
transport_tips: KTEL public buses connect the airport with Kalamata city center on a scheduled basis, though frequencies can be limited outside peak season. Taxis are readily available outside the terminal and provide a convenient option for direct transfers to city hotels or coastal resorts. Renting a car is highly recommended for travelers planning to explore the broader Messenia region and the scenic Peloponnese coastline.
local_tip: Pack a swimsuit in your carry-on if traveling in summer—the nearest beaches to the airport are just a 10-minute drive away, making it easy to start your vacation immediately upon landing without needing to stop in town first.
